events.title: Sand Creek Massacre
events.description: At dawn, about 675 Colorado volunteer soldiers attacked a peaceful encampment of Cheyenne and Arapaho people along Sand Creek in eastern Colorado. They killed more than 200 people, most of them women, children and the elderly.
events.significance: One of the darkest episodes of the American Indian Wars. It deepened mistrust between the United States and Plains nations, and it led to federal investigations and lasting calls for remembrance and accountability.

events.title: C. S. Lewis Is Born in Belfast
events.description: Clive Staples Lewis, later known as C. S. Lewis, was born in Belfast, Ireland. He became an Oxford and Cambridge scholar and a celebrated writer.
events.significance: Lewis wrote The Chronicles of Narnia, Mere Christianity and The Screwtape Letters. His fiction and essays have reached millions of readers across generations.

events.title: UN Adopts the Partition Plan for Palestine
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly passed Resolution 181 by a vote of 33 to 13, with 10 abstentions. It recommended dividing British-ruled Palestine into separate Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem under international administration.
events.significance: The vote was a turning point in the history of the Middle East. It was followed by the end of the British Mandate and the first Arab-Israeli war, and its legacy still shapes debate over the region.

events.title: Warren Commission Established
events.description: One week after the assassination of John F. Kennedy, President Lyndon B. Johnson created a commission led by Chief Justice Earl Warren. Its task was to investigate the president's death.
events.significance: The commission's 1964 report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone. Its findings have been debated ever since, and the commission remains central to public discussion of the assassination.
